content.title: Vacations won't be priority for low-end travelers in 2026: Analyst
content.description:
A record 31 million Americans are expected to take to the skies and travel this week for Thanksgiving, according to Airlines for America's data, as major airline operators recover from the US government shutdown.

Bloomberg Intelligence senior aerospace defense and airlines industry analyst George Ferguson discusses travel trends for this holiday season, commenting on his survey that illustrated lower enthusiasm for vacations in 2026.

Also catch George Ferguson weigh in on whether the US government shutdown could impact airlines' earnings for this quarter.

content.title: Airlines will need time to 'smooth out' following gov't shutdown
content.description:
While President Trump signed a federal funding bill that reopened the US government earlier this week, does this give enough time for the airline industry to bounce back and get its ducks in a row before Americans take to the skies for Thanksgiving?

The Points Guy Director of Content Eric Rosen sits down with Myles Udland on Market Domination Overtime to talk about recent flight cancellations and the advantages of TSA PreCheck ahead of the busy holiday travel season.

At Yahoo Finance Invest, Delta Air Lines (DAL) CEO Ed Bastian called the government shutdown "inexcusable" and "incredibly disruptive."

Also hear Bloomberg Intelligence senior analyst George Ferguson's thoughts on holiday travel disruptions.

To watch more expert insights and analysis on the latest market action, check out more Market Domination Overtime.
